hostCode.behaviour: A Turtle or N-Triples body is parsed into its triples, prefix declarations and base, a body that does not parse stopping at a line with the parser's sentence.
A byte order mark is stripped before the body is read and remembered so a write puts it back.
The five family findings: a re-declared prefix, a relative IRI without a base, a malformed language tag and an XSD datatype XSD does not define, shared by every reading of the body.
A body that does not parse gives only `rdf.unparseable`, which replaces every other finding.
An added triple is appended to its subject's statement as a `;` continuation matching its indentation, or written as a new statement at the end.
A removed triple takes its whole lines where it owns them, its fragment and stranded separator where it shares a line, and its statement where it is the last.
A renamed term is rewritten in every token naming it, in subject, predicate, object and datatype position, prefixed or full.
A literal object is rewritten in place, its neighbouring bytes untouched.
A new prefix is declared beside the existing declarations, after the last one.
An IRI is written prefixed under the longest declared namespace that leaves a clean local name, else bracketed.
An IRI is drawn as its prefixed name when it compresses, else as its local name.
The local name of an IRI is what follows its last '#' or '/', or the whole IRI.
A typed term is a full IRI, a bracketed IRI or a prefixed name under the file's declarations, an undeclared prefix refused by name.
A typed prefix declaration is `prefix: iri`, brackets tolerated, the IRI absolute.
Renaming onto a name the document already uses is refused, and a declaration that is not `prefix: iri` is refused with the example.
The answers to the family's prompts become edits: a declared prefix, a renamed term, a removed resource, a relation, a new resource typed `rdfs:Resource`.
Stored positions are read from the registration's `layout:` block, keyed by element id.
A stored position wins over the computed one for an element the reading draws; a stored position of an element it does not draw is ignored.
The cards stand in bands by their first type's drawn name, ordered by its bytes with the untyped band last, each a four-column grid of 280 by 160 cells in projection order, 80 between bands.
While the RDF graph reading is cut by its budget every edit is withheld.
The drawn elements are streamed to the canvas a viewport at a time, as the module's payloads.
hostCode.reason: Delivering the drawn elements to the canvas, a viewport at a time, is how the host renders what the description derives; the description states the elements and their attributes.

hostCode.behaviour: An edit is applied to the body and recorded on the host's history for undo and redo.
hostCode.reason: The history that undoes and redoes an edit is the host's; the description states the edit as model changes the binding writes.

hostCode.behaviour: Every IRI or blank node in subject or object position is a card in the order the file first names it, its literals rows and its IRI-valued types badges, every other triple between two cards an edge, a collection folded into numbered member edges, at most 1000 cards.
A collection's cons cells are followed through `rdf:first` and `rdf:rest` and stay out of the drawing.
A literal row carries its language tag with `@`, else its datatype compressed unless it is `xsd:string`.
